about: room content after a member's seat ends, where the end names the rows held good (`trusted_through`): the Constitution's proposal of 2026-11-22 for CC 2.4.1.1, for persist v62.0. Generated from models/causal_kernel/conferral_content.py; checked by check_conferral_content.py. A PROPOSAL until the Constitution rules it

cases.about: no end held: a member's content rows count and are in the room's content
cases.name: content_no_end

cases.about: a counted removal names the newest row of the member's series: the whole series behind it stays in the room's content
cases.name: removal_names_tip

cases.about: the removal's signers held none of the member's content, so it names no tip: rows that reach a reader are counted at their head and not in the room's content, until a counted row names a tip
cases.name: removal_signers_hold_nothing

cases.about: the removers had not yet held m3 when they signed (it is concurrent with the end): m3 is out for everyone, honest or not; no rule can tell which
cases.name: removal_in_flight_row

cases.about: the same rows, and then a counted row of the body names m3: tips only grow, and m3 is in the room's content from then on
cases.name: in_flight_row_named_later

cases.about: a row that adds tips names the end it extends, so no node holds it before that end: in every arrival order the door allows, the end comes first
cases.name: adding_row_waits_for_its_end

cases.about: after the removal the member signs m3 at the last head it sat at, not naming the end, and it arrives after the end at a node that never saw it: admitted, counted at its head, never in the room's content; the same answer in every arrival order
cases.name: removed_member_keeps_posting

cases.about: a content row naming a roster head later than h_e: the member's seat is ended there, and the row does not count
cases.name: row_at_later_head

cases.about: a content row that has the end in its past does not count, whatever head it names
cases.name: row_names_end

cases.about: the member's own resignation names its own newest row, which no one else holds yet: the resignation concludes at once (the seat ends; nothing waits), and when m2 arrives it and what is behind it are kept
cases.name: resignation_names_tip

cases.about: the end names a tip that never arrives: it keeps nothing, and no rule tells this end from one that names no tip, so the member's held rows are out
cases.name: end_names_tip_never_held

cases.about: the removal names m2, and m2 reaches this node after the removal: out until then, kept from then on; the same answer in every arrival order once the rows are held
cases.name: tip_arrives_after_end

cases.about: one key forked its own series (m2 and x2 both follow m1): the end names one branch, and only that branch and what is behind it stay; the other branch is out until a counted row names it
cases.name: fork_of_one_series

cases.about: the enders hold both branches of a fork and name both: tips are a set, and both branches stay
cases.name: fork_both_branches_named

cases.about: two devices forked the series (m2, x2) and a later row names both as its predecessors: one tip keeps both branches
cases.name: fork_rejoined

cases.about: the member edited its post m1 before the removal, and the edit is behind the named tip: the edit is kept with its target
cases.name: kept_post_edited_before_end

cases.about: after the removal the member signs an edit of its kept post m1 at the old head: the edit is a content row no tip names, so it is out though its target is kept. A composer does NOT follow its target into the content; if it did, an ended member would rewrite its kept posts
cases.name: kept_post_edited_after_end

cases.about: the same with a retraction: the retraction row is out of the content like any row no tip names, and it still takes effect: an author's retraction of its own row takes effect whenever it is signed, so the kept post leaves the room's content. It can only take a row out
cases.name: kept_post_retracted_after_end

cases.about: with no end held: a member retracts its own post, and the post is out
cases.name: post_retracted_no_end

cases.about: the member retracts its post from its second key: its own retraction, and it takes effect
cases.name: retraction_from_a_second_device

cases.about: a co-member signs a retraction of the member's post: not its author's, and not read by this rule
cases.name: retraction_by_a_co_member

cases.about: the member retracts its retraction: nothing is restored, or an ended member would add a row back
cases.name: retraction_of_a_retraction

cases.about: the retraction names the end (so as an act under the ended seat it does not count, E4): it is still its author's own retraction and takes effect
cases.name: retraction_that_does_not_count

cases.about: the tip m3 is held, its predecessor m2 is not, and m1 behind that is held: nothing shows m1 is m3's ancestor, so m1 is not kept until m2 arrives
cases.name: middle_of_chain_not_held

cases.about: the same, and m2 arrives: m2 and m1 are kept; the same answer in every arrival order once all three are held, m2 last included
cases.name: middle_of_chain_arrives

cases.about: the same fork, and a counted row then names the other branch's tip: both branches stay
cases.name: fork_other_branch_named_later

cases.about: the member's second key signed a series the enders never held: the end names one tip, of the first key's series, and the whole second series is out
cases.name: second_key_never_seen

cases.about: the same rows, and a counted row then names the second series' tip: it is in
cases.name: second_key_named_later

cases.about: a row signed by the member's second key names a row of its first key as its predecessor: both are the member's own, and the walk follows
cases.name: prev_across_the_members_keys

cases.about: the member's row names a CO-MEMBER's row as its predecessor, and that row names the member's m1: the walk does not pass through another member's row, so m1 is not kept
cases.name: prev_through_a_co_members_row

cases.about: two counted removals of the member at one head, concurrent, naming different tips: both are the count's word, and the kept set is the union; nothing waits
cases.name: two_removals_different_tips

cases.about: after a removal that kept m1 only, the member signs m2 and a resignation at the old head naming m2, neither naming the removal: where a counted end counts the member's own end is not read, so m2 is not added
cases.name: removal_then_backdated_resignation

cases.about: the same rows under the proposal's third point read literally (`union`): the member's own later resignation adds m2. This is the hole count_first closes
cases.name: removal_then_backdated_resignation_union

cases.about: the member signs two resignations at one head naming different tips (a fork of its own end): a row stays only where both hold it good, so a second resignation never adds a row
cases.name: two_resignations

cases.about: the member resigned naming m1, and no counted row ends the seat; a counted row then names m2: the member's own tips are still read and the counted row's are added
cases.name: resignation_then_counted_tips

cases.about: the same, and the member then signs a second resignation naming nothing: it narrows the member's own tips to none, and what the counted row named stays
cases.name: resignation_counted_tips_then_narrowing

cases.about: a row adding tips signed by the member is never read: only a counted row adds
cases.name: member_adds_tips_itself

cases.about: a second removal that has the first in its past ends nothing (the seat was already ended), but it is a counted row of the body and its tips add
cases.name: second_end_after_first

cases.about: a resignation naming a head later than the removal's h_e, concurrent with it: where a counted end counts the member's own end's tips are not read, so naming none takes nothing out
cases.name: resignation_at_later_head

cases.about: the member was removed at H1 with m2 (at H1) kept, and then signs a resignation at H0: E3 puts its own row at H1 at a head later than an end of its seat, so m2 no longer counts. An ended member can take its own rows out this way; conferral_end.py's reader's line bounds it
cases.name: backdated_resignation_uncounts_own_rows

cases.about: E1: an end naming H0 with H1 in its own past concludes nothing, and its tips are not read
cases.name: end_stale_head

cases.about: the end names as a tip a row at a head later than h_e: naming it does not make it count (E3 decides first), and what is behind it at h_e is kept
cases.name: tip_at_later_head

cases.about: the member left with m1 kept, was admitted again at HA, and posts n1 there: a new seat with no end, so n1 is in the room's content; m1 stays on the first end's word
cases.name: rejoin_and_post

cases.about: a re-admission restores nothing: m2, which the first end did not hold good, stays out after the member is seated again
cases.name: rejoin_restores_nothing

cases.about: a row signed after the re-admission that names the OLD head: the head a row names decides, so it is a row of the old seat and is out; the device signs again at a current head
cases.name: stale_device_after_rejoin

cases.about: a row naming a head at which the member does not sit (after its end, before the re-admission): it belongs to no seat and does not count
cases.name: row_between_seats

cases.about: the removal is the member's end and a version of the roster: a row of the member that names it as its head names a head at which the member is out, and does not count; a version built on the removal admits the member again and a row there is in a new seat
cases.name: row_naming_the_removal_as_its_head

cases.about: the hole a second seat would open: the member rejoins, posts n1 naming m2 (which the first end left out) as its predecessor, and leaves again with n1 as the tip. The walk does not cross seats: n1 is kept, m2 stays out
cases.name: second_seat_tip_reaches_left_out_row

cases.about: the same where the first end kept m2: it stays in, on the first end's word and not the second's
cases.name: second_seat_tip_reaches_kept_row

cases.about: the second seat ends and its end holds nothing good: the second seat's rows are out, and the first seat's kept rows are untouched
cases.name: second_seat_ends_without_tips

cases.about: a counted row adds a tip for the FIRST end after the member has rejoined: it cites that end, so it is read in the first seat, and m2 comes in
cases.name: keeps_first_end_after_rejoin

cases.about: the first end's adding row names a row of the second seat as a tip: a tip holds good only rows of its own seat, so after the second seat ends without it, n1 is out
cases.name: first_end_names_second_seat_row

cases.about: two removals of the first seat, naming different tips, both arriving after the rejoin: they are ends of the first seat by the head they name; their tips join there, and the second seat is not ended
cases.name: two_first_seat_ends_after_rejoin

cases.about: after rejoining, the member signs a resignation at the old head naming nothing: it is an end of the old seat, where a counted end counts and its own end is not read; the second seat is not ended by it
cases.name: backdated_resignation_after_rejoin

cases.about: seated again, the member retracts a post of its first seat that the first end kept: a retraction is read across seats, and the post leaves the content
cases.name: retract_old_post_after_rejoin

cases.about: a tip that is not a content row of the member is not read: here the end names a roster head as a tip, and nothing is held good
cases.name: tip_not_the_members

merge: whose tips are read: count_first (the reference's default), union (the proposal's third point read literally) or count_first_self_union; see `rules`. The Constitution rules which
refused: null in every case here: every content row names its head

roles.B: a key of the member whose seat ends
roles.B2: a second key of the same member
roles.M: a co-member: its rows are not this member's content and get no answer here
roles.count: a counted row (a roster version, a removal, a row adding tips)

rules:
end_void.stale_head  E1: the end has a head later than h_e in its own past: it concludes nothing
    end_void.seat_ended  the end has a counting end of the seat in its own past: the seat was already ended
Whether an end counts is decided by its own causal past alone, so no row signed later changes it. In
particular the member's own end is NOT voided for naming a head later than another end's: under that rule the
exhaustive check found the member reviving a row that named its first resignation, by signing a second one at
an older head. An extra end of the member's own only ever takes rows out (E3, E4, and the rule below).

Whose tips are read (`merge`). The proposal's third point read literally is `union`, and
check_conferral_content.py shows that under it an ended member adds content for ever, by signing a further
resignation at the head it last sat at. The reference's default closes that:
    count_first             (default) the count's word: the union of the tips of every counted end that is not
                            stale and of every counted `tips` row. The member's own ends are read only where no
                            counted end counts, and then a row stays only where EVERY one of them holds it
                            good, so a second resignation can remove but never add. A `tips` row signed by the
                            member is never read.
    union                   the union of the tips of every end that counts, the member's own included, and of
                            every counted `tips` row
    count_first_self_union  count_first, but where only the member's own ends speak, the union of them

Rules for a content row, in the order they decide (the name a failing test reports):
    no_seat          the row names a head at which the member does not sit: not counted
    no_end           no end counts: counted and in force
    E4.names_end     the row has a counting end in its past: not counted
    E3.later_head    the row names a head that has a counting end's h_e in its past: the seat is ended there
    W.retracted      counted, not in force: a retraction of the row by the member, under any of its keys, is
                     held (a person retracts from a second device). The Constitution's ruling of 2026-11-22:
                     an author's retraction of its own row takes effect whenever it is signed, before or after
                     an end, whether or not the retraction itself counts or is kept, and a retraction of a
                     retraction restores nothing. It can only take a row out. A co-member's is not read
    T.held_good      counted and in force: a held tip that is read, or its ancestor along `prev` among the
                     member's own rows, by any of its keys
    E2.forward       counted at its own head, not in force: not held good
